:::{#def-surprisal-under}
#### Surprisal under a mass function or density

Let $X$ be a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable),
and let $q$ be a [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) or [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf)
on the possible values of $X$.
The **surprisal under $q$** of a possible value $x$ of $X$ is

$$\surprisalunderf{q}{x} \eqdef -\log q(x),$$

with $-\log 0 \eqdef \infty$.
It is the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) (or its [continuous](#def-surprisal-continuous) form) that $x$ would have
if $q$ were the [mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) or density of $X$,
whether or not it is.
Evaluating $\surprisalunderf{q}{\cdot}$ at $X$ itself gives the [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $\surprisalunderf{q}{X}$,
whose value is $\surprisalunderf{q}{x}$ when $X = x$.

:::
